subject: Fitting pharmacokinetic concentration curves with uncertain injection time

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Fitting pharmacokinetic concentration curves with uncertain injection time
parts:
We use Stan to  fit pharmacokinetic concentration curves with an injection time that is known only approximately, e.g. in the range from 90 to 110 seconds. I know that the simulated curve shown above could be analyzed by conventional procedures, but this is a simplified example. The real study data are generated by two overlapping injections, can be more noisy, and the study has a complex cross-over design that will be included in a hierarchical model. nlme and friends fail here even when the injection time is assumed known.

When I try to estimate the unknown injection time as in the attached program, convergence is not good, and I get a few:;

There were 952 transitions after warmup that exceeded the maximum treedepth

I assume that I have to do some manual log_increment tweaking for this case as I can see from similar changepoint examples, but I could not find out how to do this.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fitting pharmacokinetic concentration curves with uncertain injection time

Hi Dieter,

The maximum treedepth issue is something you should address. You can start by increasing the maximum treedepth and lowering the initial stepsize. You'll have to find out how to adjust those arguments in the particular interface you're using.

Regarding the Stan program, there isn't enough in your post to understand how you've modeled your injection time. If you want to send the whole program, I might be able to see the problem. In particular, I don't know if you've included the injection time into the ode function, if it's outside, or if you've found some way to integrate it out (that seems hard, though).




Daniel

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fitting pharmacokinetic concentration curves with uncertain injection time
parts:
Thanks, Daniel,

we normally use the Bayesian versions of nonmem to model pharmakokinetic data, but it also has problems with unknown injection times - with the exception of one overall delay that can be easily modelled.

With the real data, we know that the injection time is 100 and 400 seconds, but from the data one can easily see that there is a transport-lag (not a diffusion lag) of between 10 and 20 seconds, and additional lags between tissues.

For a first look at the data, I tried a simplified analysis by fitting overlapping exponentials with prior-constrained onset; no ode or other differential equations involved, code exaclty as given. In the simulated example, I put a prior on the lag and tried to estimate it.

However, this brings Stan to a crawl, and I was not sure estimating a parameter with a discontinuity is a valid approach at all.

Dieter

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fitting pharmacokinetic concentration curves with uncertain injection time
parts:
Thanks to Daniel and Bob, who both jumped into the pharmacokinetics = differential equation trap. Probably I was not clear enough that we use nonmem for diff-equations, but my question was related to seemingly simple curve-fitting problem.

I had forgotten that a interpolation of the original sampled values is needed to get a smooth gradient when position in time are unknown. Thanks to edbaskerville and Daniel Lee # https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/58 who solved the problem of floor-casting to int in stan using a bisection algorithm "in frightening glory".

The code works, but is terribly slow. I did not try to optimize anything. Currrently, it is limited to equidistant time points of sampling rate 1, and I do not think I will follow up this path until there is a decent way to interpolate.

Dieter
